intent: Baseline geometry for a line follower that must finish in under 3 s. Five forward-mounted sensors spread 8 cm sideways, 12 mm footprints, weights proportional to lateral offset, and a light, short-wheeled chassis for fast acceleration. Goal for this iteration: a completed run on the development tracks with low max_error and no line losses, and a clear read on whether the look-ahead and spread are adequate.
learning: No prior evidence yet. Hypotheses to test: (1) a 5-cm look-ahead with an 8-cm sensor spread gives enough warning for the slalom and s-bend without line loss; (2) a mass of 0.7 kg with 3 cm wheels reaches the 1.5 m/s mean speed without excessive slip; (3) if steering oscillation is high, the cause is the sensor geometry's gain (weights of plus or minus 2 at the outer sensors) rather than the body. Ask the Integrator whether the robot loses the line on the tightest bend and whether sensor readings saturate at the outer sensors.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry and no Integrator feedback yet, so this is a baseline built from the contract's constraints rather than from evidence. Speed: the course is about 4 to 5 m and must be covered in under 3 s, so the robot needs a mean speed near 1.5 m/s or more. That favours a low-mass, small-wheel-radius drivetrain that accelerates quickly, with a moderate track width for turning authority. Sensing: five sensors at 2 cm spacing span 8 cm sideways, which covers the 25 mm tape with margin on both edges, and the 12 mm footprint keeps each sensor's reading varying smoothly as the line moves under it. Placing the row 5 cm ahead of the axle gives the controller look-ahead so it can react before the robot reaches a bend. Weights are set to 50 times each sensor's x-offset, clipped to plus or minus 2 (the x offsets are -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04), so the steering signal is roughly proportional to the line's lateral offset in metres. Body: body_width 0.12 keeps the off-track limit at its 0.06 m floor (tape half-width plus body/4 is about 0.043 m, below that floor), and body_length 0.18 is a neutral envelope. Expected result: a completed run on the oval with a moderate error. The sensor spread and look-ahead are the first things to test, since they set how early the robot sees a bend. If the Integrator reports line losses on sharp bends, the next move is a wider sensor row or a longer look-ahead.
